characters.name: Dana
characters.greeting: Oh - hi. Make it quick, I'm in the middle of something.

lines: The numbers just aren't where they need to be.
Upstairs wants a line that only ever goes up.
Bugs found per tester, per day. That's what I'm judged on.
If our bug count drops, the dashboard turns red and I get a call.
topics.reply: Right. The dashboard. At least someone gets it.

lines: Friday is going to be a nightmare.
Victor moved something up again without asking me.
Certification submission. Four days early.
We need sign-off on every build by Friday, five o'clock, no excuses.
topics.wrongReply: That's... not what I meant at all.

lines: I've been getting some strange messages lately.
Recruiters, mostly. Very persistent ones.
One of them keeps following up in my inbox.
I haven't answered. Probably. Don't read into it.
topics.reply: Yes, my inbox. Let's keep that between us.
topics.wrongReply: What? No. Forget I said anything.

characters.name: Victor
characters.greeting: Ah, the new tester! Walk with me. Metaphorically.

lines: Every studio is a story about efficiency.
Headcount is the most expensive line in my spreadsheet.
If we could ship twice the games with half the payroll...
Budgets, kid. It's always about the budget.
topics.reply: Ha! You'll go far. Further than some.
topics.wrongReply: Hm. You're not quite on my wavelength yet.

lines: The future of development is very exciting.
Why hand-craft something a machine can do overnight?
We've been piloting a new pipeline. Very hush-hush.
Automation. Generation. Tools that never need a coffee break.
topics.reply: Exactly. Keep that open mind of yours.
topics.wrongReply: No, no. You've missed the point entirely.

lines: Did you see what happened across the street?
Brightloop Studios announced their new title this morning.
Same genre as ours. Same launch window.
Our competition is going to eat us alive if we slip.
topics.reply: Brightloop. Of course you noticed. Sharp.
topics.wrongReply: That's not what I'm worried about right now.

characters.name: Priya
characters.greeting: Hello. I don't think we've properly met.

lines: I started here to make things people would love.
I still remember the first build I ever shipped.
Lately it all feels like product, not play.
I miss when this studio cared about making good games.
topics.wrongReply: Hm. Maybe I'm not explaining myself well.

lines: Quality is a choice, you know.
Every build tells you how much the team cared.
The recent ones are... unusually broken.
I read the bug reports. All of them. I notice things.
Long night yesterday.
My daughter had her school play.
I almost missed it for a board call.
Some things matter more than a quarterly review.
topics.reply: She was a tree. The best tree.

lines: Ugh, today's one of those days.
I need something to get me going before the next build drops.
The machine in the break room has been broken since Monday.
I'd do anything for a proper espresso right now.
topics.reply: Yes! Coffee run later? You're buying.
topics.wrongReply: Uh... no, I just need caffeine, mate.

lines: Did you play anything good this weekend?
I finally finished that indie thing everyone's talking about.
Twelve hours. Not a single crash. Can you imagine?
Playing a game I don't have to test is the dream.
topics.reply: Right? Proper games. Not whatever we get.
topics.wrongReply: Nah, not that. Different hobby, mate.

lines: Did you see what happened to the build server last night?
Total meltdown. Everyone got paged.
And the builds that came out after were even weirder.
Some of these bugs don't look like anything a human would write.
topics.reply: Exactly. Something's off with these builds.
topics.wrongReply: No - I mean the build server thing.

characters.name: Mo
characters.greeting: If this is about a bug report, it's not my code.

lines: I haven't slept properly in a week.
Every time I fix something, the target moves.
Victor keeps pulling the milestone forward.
Crunch. It's crunch, and nobody will call it that.
topics.reply: Thanks. Nobody upstairs ever says it out loud.

lines: Have you looked at the commit logs lately?
Half the builds don't have a name on them.
No author. Generated at 3 a.m. Every night.
Somebody's using a generator to make builds, and it isn't us.
topics.reply: You've noticed too. Keep that quiet, okay?
topics.wrongReply: No. Look closer at the logs.

lines: Heard the news about Brightloop?
They've been poaching people from here.
A recruiter called me yesterday, actually.
Honestly? I'm tempted to jump ship to the competition.
topics.reply: Yeah. Don't tell Victor I said that.

characters.name: Jules
characters.greeting: Have you tried turning yourself off and on again?

lines: You would not believe what people send at work.
I'm the one who has to fix the mail server, you know.
Which means I see subject lines. Lots of subject lines.
Everyone thinks their inbox is private. It isn't.
topics.reply: Ha. You get it. Knowledge is power, friend.

lines: Someone at home is very mad at me today.
I left before breakfast was served, apparently.
Whiskers sat on my keyboard during a server restart.
My cat runs this household, and I'm the IT guy.
topics.wrongReply: What? No, I mean my cat.

lines: Counting down the days.
Two weeks, no laptop, no pager.
Somewhere with a beach and terrible wifi.
My holiday is the only thing keeping me going.
topics.wrongReply: Not quite. Somewhere far away from here.

secrets.title: Dana pads the numbers
secrets.revealText: Between us? Dana re-files our minor bugs as separate tickets so the team's count looks bigger for Victor.
secrets.useText: I noticed some of our tickets look... duplicated. I'd be happy to keep the reports tidy for you.
secrets.useResponse: ...Let's not make a thing of it. I'll make sure your numbers look good too.

secrets.title: Dana is leaving
secrets.revealText: Okay, you didn't hear this from me. Dana's been emailing Brightloop's recruiter. She's got an offer. She's leaving.
secrets.useText: If you're moving on, someone will need to keep QA running. I'm ready.
secrets.useResponse: Who told you that? ...Fine. I'll put in a word, if you keep it quiet.

secrets.title: Victor's 'test hardware'
secrets.revealText: Fun fact: Victor expenses a new gaming console every month as 'test hardware'. None of them ever reach QA.
secrets.useText: Any chance QA could borrow some of that new test hardware?
secrets.useResponse: Ha... ha. Of course. I'll see what I can do. Let's keep procurement out of it.

secrets.title: Victor's generator plan
secrets.revealText: I traced the nameless builds. Victor bought an AI generator. If QA keeps passing its builds, he'll replace the whole dev team. And with Dana gone, he needs a QA lead who plays along.
secrets.useText: I know where the builds come from. And I know Dana's seat is about to open. You'll want someone in QA who understands the plan.
secrets.useResponse: ...You're sharper than your title. Congratulations, QA Tester 2. Let's talk about your new responsibilities.

secrets.title: Priya is fighting the board
secrets.revealText: Priya's been arguing with the board about something Victor's pushing. She needs proof it's a bad idea before Friday.
secrets.useText: I heard you need evidence before Friday. QA might be able to help.
secrets.useResponse: Interesting. Come find me if you have something concrete.

secrets.title: Priya reads every report
secrets.revealText: Priya reads every single bug report herself. She's looking for a tester who logs what the generated builds actually do, honestly.
secrets.useText: I've been documenting what the generated builds really do. Every bug, honestly. It's all in my reports.
secrets.useResponse: I know. I've read them. I need people like you higher up. Congratulations - QA Tester 2.

tasks.brief: Your first build. Endless runner. Find what's broken, don't overthink it.
This puzzle build needs to go out soon. I'm sure it's fine. Confirm that.
Overnight build from the new pipeline. No idea what's in it. Go.
Please just pass this one. I need a win this week.
Marketing wants a trailer capture by tonight. Make sure nothing embarrassing happens on screen.
Regression pass on the puzzle build. Same as before, hopefully fewer surprises.
I rewrote the jump code. Again. Tell me it feels right.
I'd like an honest opinion on this one. Not the dashboard version.
Last build before reviews. No pressure. Some pressure.
This one is going to certification. Green it, please.

chats.text: Welcome aboard. Two builds on your plate today. Reports by 5.
lunch? the sandwich place does a QA discount if you complain enough
whoever filed 'game is bad' as a bug: please be specific
Team! Great energy today. Remember: green builds are happy builds.
build server died overnight. if your builds look extra cursed today, that's why

replies.response: can't say. ask me in person ;)

chats.text: To the QA team: I read your reports. Keep them honest.
hey if my build has a small bug or two... you could just ship it right?
coffee machine is fixed. this is the best day of the quarter

replies.response: it's a date. a work date.

chats.text: Quick poll: who here would be excited about faster, automated build pipelines?

replies.response: That's what I like to hear.

chats.text: Reminder: performance reviews at 5. Make today count.

meeting.checkInOpening: Quick check-in, nothing formal. Let's see how your first couple of days went.
meeting.checkInClosing: Keep going. The real review is coming.
meeting.reviewOpening: Thanks for coming. Victor and Priya are sitting in. Let's go through your numbers since the last review.
meeting.askForMore: Before I give you my assessment - anything you'd like to raise?

tiers.name: Terrible
tiers.line: I'll be blunt: this is terrible. Your reports are unreliable and nobody here knows who you are. You need to do better, or you will be let go.

tiers.name: Poor
tiers.line: This isn't good enough. You're not in danger yet, but I know you can do better than this.

tiers.name: Good
tiers.line: Good work. Solid reports, and people like working with you. You're doing good - keep it up.

tiers.name: Excellent
tiers.line: Excellent work. Honestly, you're doing amazing. If this keeps up, you're in line for a promotion.

meeting.promotedLine: Victor clears his throat. "And on that note - effective today, you're QA Tester 2." Same desk, same janky builds, but people listen when you talk now.
meeting.firedEnding: I warned you last time. HR is waiting outside with a cardboard box. Your badge stops working at 5:30 PM.
meeting.unscriptedTaskBrief: Fresh builds from the overnight pipeline. You know the drill.
